unitChecks.reason: Source: Shi Hu again sent Shi Cheng to attack Fancheng, failed, then advanced and took Guangcheng; EN omits again (又).
Source: though Huang styled himself King of Yan without court mandate, he sent Liu Xiang to report victory, explain provisional authority, and request a Central Plain campaign.

Source: moreover Huang learned Yu Liang died and Bing and Yi succeeded as generals-ministers, then memorialized on muddled vs clear rulers who elevate the worthy together; EN drops 又 and softens 继为将相/昏明.
Source: favoring kin and the empresss clan brings sure overthrow and humiliation; both fields cover the conditional disaster.
Source: Shen Bo of Zhou was called a worthy maternal uncle because he was enfeoffed outside and did not hold court power.
Source: even capable King Zhao of Qin trusted two maternal uncles and nearly disordered the state.
Source: Emperor Wu of Han elevated Tian Fen so every vital affair was decided through him.
Source: after Tian Fen died the emperor gnashed teeth in after-the-fact regret.
Source: weak Emperor Cheng, confused by a beautiful wife and indulging five maternal uncles, let Wang Mang take the throne without effort.
Source: each time one reads these affairs, who would not feel pain and regret.
Source: if maternal uncles were as worthy as Marquis of Rang and Wang Feng, one hears of two ministers not two lords.
Source: if they lacked talent, there followed disasters like Dou Xian and Liang Ji.
Source: all these successes and failures are already thus clear as a lesson.
Source: if one can change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided; EN adds in time, which Chinese does not state.
Source: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age and should exalt Jins Way, yet meets many state hardships, with deep grief pressing and past affairs still burning; EN merges 命世天挺 into one gloss.

Source: tracing the cause, late Minister of Works Yu Liang as chief maternal uncle held heavy power, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals so Su Jun and Zu Yue ruined the state; EN adds harshly.
Source links Empress Dowager indignation with 一旦升遐; temporal force of 至今 and exact death implication stay difficult; keep uncertainty explicit.
Source: if altars were not numinous and men and spirits gave no aid, would wolfish hearts have been allowed to reach their limit.

Source: past events if not forgotten are a model for later affairs, yet Bing as Zhongshu jian and Left General with fellows holds central pivot and outer commands, brothers side by side unmatched; EN drops 不忘.
Source: Your Majesty deeply honors Weiyang maternal-uncle ties; Bing and others ought themselves to stretch necks in expectation; EN replaces 渭阳 with generic family ties.

Source: Huang often asks why not enfeoff maternal clan with vassal states, enrich stipends and gifts, and limit power and advantage so there is no partial favor above or private talk below; EN turns 何不 into an imperative and drops 利.
Source: thus from what would honor and disgrace arise.
Source: from what words would slander and calumny spring.
Source: formerly Yu Liang alone already had standing yet still brought age-change; how much more todays office-holders who from the first had no renown.
Source: human feelings are easily confused and hard to announce door to door; even if Your Majesty has no partiality toward them, who in the realm would say there is none.
Source: servant and Bing and others differ in rank and are far apart in situation; as close imperial kin they warrant deference to circumstances; EN drops 等 and reorders speakers.
Source: Huang alone presses contrary speech for the emperor above and for Bings sake below, despising accommodating ministers and judging gain and loss.
Source: if one does not right what is overturned, of what use is that minister.
Source: Xu Fu warned of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow, so loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage because inspection was careless and prevention not begun early.
Source: what the servant now sets forth may be called prevention at the first sign.
Source: only fear the emperor may not understand loyalty or use the plan, and after the affair pass again stand amid charred wreckage.
Source: Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang never failed to denounce the Wang clan in sealed memorials, so both ended dead or punished.
Source: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated without direct answer, preserved themselves and escaped, and drew the ages ridicule.

Source: disheveled-hair foreign general worries day and night how to repay, can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and sincerity to answer state grace; EN truncates the closing clauses.
Source: if the servant does not speak, who will speak.

Source: Huang also wrote Bing that by empress-chamber and maternal closeness he holds the pivot, issues and receives royal commands, holds general and provincial posts, and brothers spread a net across the capital region.
Source: since Qin and Han, has there been such extreme splendor as this.
Source: in Huang's view, if merit is achieved and affairs succeed Bing will enjoy Shen Bo's name.
Source: if not, Bing will not escape the track of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.
Source: histories show maternal kin pampered into holding power and disordering court—first surpassing glory then the unfit-rider burden; love thereby suffices to harm.
Source: Huang resents rulers who failed the art of preventing sprouts while keeping final favor; why not establish a territorial fief and hereditary vassal states like Zhou Qi and Chen.
Source: then they would forever keep south-facing honor with no worry of dismissal and disgrace.
Source: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and emptied/humbled themselves.
Source: worthies gave them their hearts; though endangered by eunuchs the realm lamented them because they conducted themselves without arrogance and gave their lives for the state.
Source: now the four seas hang inverted, usurping rebels flee within China, families have blood-soaked grievances and men vengeance-regret; how can one rest easy talking elegantly through the year.

Source: though deficient in virtue Huang received former-emperor general appointment; with several commanderies he still seeks to swallow strong enemies, fighting three seasons and farming one yet troops unexhausted, grain surplus, enemies daily more afraid and borders wider—imperial majesty cannot be compared in the same year.
Source: Bing saw memorial and letter, was greatly afraid; because Huang was extremely far and beyond control, with He Chong and others he memorialized to permit Huang to style himself King of Yan.
Source: that year Huang campaigned against Goguryeo; King Zhao begged a covenant and Huang returned; EN reduces 乞盟 to sued for peace.
Source: next year Zhao sent his heir apparent to pay court to Huang.
Source: after Duan Liaos defeat Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui, feared his long-shaken fame would not let him survive intact, and feigned madness with wanton drink, loose hair, song and shouts.
Source: Gui believed and did not restrain him, so Han could roam at will and practiced mountain-river forms and crucial attack roads thoroughly.
Source: Huang sent merchant Wang Che secretly to observe Han; Han seeing Che said nothing and only stroked his breast.
Source: Che returned and reported; Huang said Han wishes to come; quotation boundary preserved.
Source: Huang had Che present bow and arrows; Han then stole fine horses, took his two sons, and returned.

Source: planning against the Shi, Huang calmly told generals Shi Hu trusts Anle and the other cities heavy defenses so north and south of the city lack preparations; a deceitful route unexpected could break all northern Ji; EN misstates north/south of the wall and whole Ji plain, and drops 从容/诡路.
Source: led 20,000 cavalry out Yeweng Pass, drove to Ji city, crossed Wusui Ford into Gaoyang, burned stores along the way, and plundered-relocated over 30,000 households from You and Ji.
Source: had Yang Yu, Tang Zhu and others build Longcheng, construct palace and temples, and change Liucheng into Longcheng county.

Source: Emperor Cheng sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang palace attendant, grand commander of military affairs north of the Yellow River, grand general, and King of Yan, other offices unchanged; EN drops concurrent Grand Herald and bearing credentials.
Source: enfeoffed various meritorious ministers, more than a hundred persons.
Source: in Xiankang 7 Huang moved the capital to Longcheng.

Source: led 40,000 picked troops in from the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo; had Han and son Chui as vanguard; sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others with 15,000 advancing from Beizhi; EN drops 长史 and 等.
Source: King Zhao thought Huang came by the northern route, so sent brother Wu with 50,000 picked troops to block Beizhi and personally led weak troops to guard the southern defile; EN drops 精锐.
Source: Han fought Zhao at Mudi, greatly defeated them, rode the victory into Wandu; Zhao fled on a single horse.
Source: Huang dug Zhao father Lis tomb, loaded the corpse with mother, wife and treasures, plundered over 50,000 men and women, burned palaces, destroyed Wandu and returned.
Source: next year Zhao sent envoys declaring subject status with local products, and Huang then returned the fathers corpse.
Source: Yuwen Gui sent state chancellor Moqian Hun to campaign against Huang; generals asked to fight and Huang refused; EN omits 国相.
Source: Hun took Huang to fear them, indulged wine and hunting, and again set no defenses.
Source: Huang said Huns extravagance and overweening already extreme, now one battle is possible; quotation preserved.
Source: sent Han with cavalry to strike; Hun greatly defeated, barely escaped alone, and their host was wholly captured.
Source: Huang personally toured prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised Longcheng palace towers; EN drops 躬.
Source: soon again led 20,000 cavalry personally against Yuwen Gui, with Han and Chui as vanguard.

Source: Gui had cavalry general Sheyiyu exhaust the host against Han; Huang sent word Sheyiyu is fierce and bold so slightly avoid him until the foe grows arrogant then take them; EN mistranslates 小避 as spar lightly.
Source: Han said Guis picked troops are all here; if defeated now Gui can be destroyed without tiring the army.
Source: Sheyiyu has only empty fame and is easy to deal with; one ought not loose the enemy and blunt army spirit.
Source: they advanced, beheaded Sheyiyu, wholly captured the host; Gui fled far to the northern desert; EN makes Huang drive him rather than Gui flee.
Source: Huang opened over a thousand li, moved their division people over 50,000 settlements (落) to Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu city Weide; EN turns 落 into dependents.
Source: performed the drink-on-arrival victory rite and discussed merit with graded rewards.

additionalCorrections.before: Shi Hu sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
additionalCorrections.after: Shi Hu again sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 季龍又使石成入攻凡城，不克，進陷廣城。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Shi Hu again sent Shi Cheng to attack Fancheng, failed, then advanced and took Guangcheng; EN omits again (又).

additionalCorrections.before: When Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi held power, he submitted a memorial: I have studied wise and foolish rulers of past ages. When they favored the worthy and elevated them together, the realm rose to peace;
additionalCorrections.after: Moreover, when Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi had succeeded as generals and ministers, he submitted a memorial: Your servant has closely observed the muddled and clear rulers of former ages; if they could treat the worthy with intimacy and elevate them together, then merit reached peaceful ascendancy;
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 又聞庾亮薨，弟冰、翼繼為將相，乃表曰：臣究觀前代昏明之主，若能親賢並建，則功致升平；
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: moreover Huang learned Yu Liang died and Bing and Yi succeeded as generals-ministers, then memorialized on muddled vs clear rulers who elevate the worthy together; EN drops 又 and softens 继为将相/昏明.

additionalCorrections.before: Change course in time and collapse can be avoided.
additionalCorrections.after: If one could change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: if one can change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided; EN adds in time, which Chinese does not state.

additionalCorrections.before: Your Majesty is heaven-born to exalt Jin's Way, yet the state has met repeated calamity; grief presses on every side, and recalling the past still burns.
additionalCorrections.after: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side, and recalling past affairs still burns with anguish to this day.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age and should exalt Jins Way, yet meets many state hardships, with deep grief pressing and past affairs still burning; EN merges 命世天挺 into one gloss.

additionalCorrections.before: The root cause was the late Minister of Works Yu Liang: as chief maternal uncle he wielded overwhelming power, judged subordinates harshly, and insulted frontier generals until Su Jun and Zu Yue, unable to bear their rage, ruined the state.
additionalCorrections.after: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: tracing the cause, late Minister of Works Yu Liang as chief maternal uncle held heavy power, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals so Su Jun and Zu Yue ruined the state; EN adds harshly.

additionalCorrections.before: Remembering past events provides a guide for the future. Yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows control the central levers of government within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side in office, with no other ministers to match them.
additionalCorrections.after: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: past events if not forgotten are a model for later affairs, yet Bing as Zhongshu jian and Left General with fellows holds central pivot and outer commands, brothers side by side unmatched; EN drops 不忘.

additionalCorrections.before: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.
additionalCorrections.after: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and his fellows ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Your Majesty deeply honors Weiyang maternal-uncle ties; Bing and others ought themselves to stretch necks in expectation; EN replaces 渭阳 with generic family ties.

additionalCorrections.before: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in vassal states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
additionalCorrections.after: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Huang often asks why not enfeoff maternal clan with vassal states, enrich stipends and gifts, and limit power and advantage so there is no partial favor above or private talk below; EN turns 何不 into an imperative and drops 利.

additionalCorrections.before: Bing and I differ in rank and are far apart in our positions; moreover, he and his brothers are close relatives of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
additionalCorrections.after: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: servant and Bing and others differ in rank and are far apart in situation; as close imperial kin they warrant deference to circumstances; EN drops 等 and reorders speakers.

additionalCorrections.before: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold supreme command, worry day and night how to repay the state, and can only destroy enemies abroad and offer loyal remonstrance within.
additionalCorrections.after: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold the rank of supreme general, worry day and night and know not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: disheveled-hair foreign general worries day and night how to repay, can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and sincerity to answer state grace; EN truncates the closing clauses.

additionalCorrections.before: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao sued for peace and he withdrew.
additionalCorrections.after: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao begged a covenant and he withdrew.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 其年皝伐高句麗，王釗乞盟而還。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: that year Huang campaigned against Goguryeo; King Zhao begged a covenant and Huang returned; EN reduces 乞盟 to sued for peace.

additionalCorrections.before: Planning against the Shi, he told his commanders, “Shi Hu trusts his garrisons at Anle and neglects the open country north and south of the wall—a sudden raid could overrun the whole Ji plain.”
additionalCorrections.after: Huang was about to plan against the Shi clan; he calmly told the generals: “Shi Hu thinks the cities of Anle and the rest are strictly and heavily guarded, and surely sets no defenses north and south of the city; now if we take a deceitful route and strike where he does not expect, the whole northern territory of Ji can be broken.”
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝將圖石氏，從容謂諸將曰：「石季龍自以安樂諸城守防嚴重，城之南北必不設備，今若詭路出其不意，冀之北土盡可破也。」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: planning against the Shi, Huang calmly told generals Shi Hu trusts Anle and the other cities heavy defenses so north and south of the city lack preparations; a deceitful route unexpected could break all northern Ji; EN misstates north/south of the wall and whole Ji plain, and drops 从容/诡路.

additionalCorrections.before: Emperor Cheng then sent Guo Xi to invest him as palace attendant, grand commander north of the river, grand general, and king of Yan, leaving other posts unchanged.
additionalCorrections.after: Emperor Cheng then sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, and King of Yan, leaving the rest of his offices as before.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 於是成帝使兼大鴻臚郭希持節拜皝侍中、大都督河北諸軍事、大將軍、燕王，其餘官皆如故。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Emperor Cheng sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang palace attendant, grand commander of military affairs north of the Yellow River, grand general, and King of Yan, other offices unchanged; EN drops concurrent Grand Herald and bearing credentials.

additionalCorrections.before: He took forty thousand veterans through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and Murong Chui as van while Wang Yu led fifteen thousand from Beizhi.
additionalCorrections.after: He took forty thousand picked soldiers through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and his son Murong Chui as vanguard, and sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others leading fifteen thousand to advance from Beizhi.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 率勁卒四萬，入自南陝，以伐宇文、高句麗，又使翰及子垂為前鋒，遣長史王寓等勒眾萬五千，從北置而進。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: led 40,000 picked troops in from the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo; had Han and son Chui as vanguard; sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others with 15,000 advancing from Beizhi; EN drops 长史 and 等.

additionalCorrections.before: King Gao Zhao assumed the main thrust would come from the north, sent fifty thousand under his brother Wu to Beizhi, and held the southern defile with weaker troops.
additionalCorrections.after: King Gao Zhao assumed Huang’s army was coming by the northern route, so he sent his younger brother Wu leading fifty thousand picked troops to block Beizhi, and personally led weaker troops to guard the southern defile.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 高句麗王釗謂皝軍之從北路也，乃遣其弟武統精銳五萬距北置，躬率弱卒以防南陝。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: King Zhao thought Huang came by the northern route, so sent brother Wu with 50,000 picked troops to block Beizhi and personally led weak troops to guard the southern defile; EN drops 精锐.

additionalCorrections.before: Yuwen Gui sent Moqian Hun; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
additionalCorrections.after: Yuwen Gui sent his state chancellor Moqian Hun against Huang; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 宇文歸遣其國相莫淺渾伐皝，諸將請戰，皝不許。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Yuwen Gui sent state chancellor Moqian Hun to campaign against Huang; generals asked to fight and Huang refused; EN omits 国相.

additionalCorrections.before: Murong Huang toured his domains, pushed farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
additionalCorrections.after: Murong Huang personally toured his prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝躬巡郡縣，勸課農桑，起龍城宮闕。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Huang personally toured prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised Longcheng palace towers; EN drops 躬.

additionalCorrections.before: Yuwen Gui sent Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han; Huang sent word: “Sheyiyu is fierce—spar lightly until he grows reckless, then strike.”
additionalCorrections.after: Yuwen Gui sent his cavalry general Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han with the whole host; Huang sent word at a gallop: “Sheyiyu is fierce and bold; you ought to avoid him a little, wait until the bandits grow arrogant, then take them.”
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 歸使其騎將涉奕於盡眾距翰，皝馳遣謂翰曰：「奕於雄悍，宜小避之，待虜勢驕，然後取也。」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Gui had cavalry general Sheyiyu exhaust the host against Han; Huang sent word Sheyiyu is fierce and bold so slightly avoid him until the foe grows arrogant then take them; EN mistranslates 小避 as spar lightly.

additionalCorrections.before: He attacked, slew Sheyiyu, took his army, and drove Yuwen Gui deep into the steppe.
additionalCorrections.after: He then advanced to battle, beheaded Sheyiyu, and wholly captured their host; Gui fled far to the northern desert.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 於是前戰，斬奕於，盡俘其眾，歸遠遁漠北。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: they advanced, beheaded Sheyiyu, wholly captured the host; Gui fled far to the northern desert; EN makes Huang drive him rather than Gui flee.

additionalCorrections.before: He annexed a thousand li of pasture, resettled fifty thousand Yuwen dependents at Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu’s fort Weide.
additionalCorrections.after: He opened over a thousand li of territory, moved more than fifty thousand of their tribal settlements to Changli, and changed Sheyiyu city to Weide city.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝開地千餘里，徙其部人五萬餘落于昌黎，改涉奕於城為威德城。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Source: Huang opened over a thousand li, moved their division people over 50,000 settlements (落) to Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu city Weide; EN turns 落 into dependents.

sourceIssues.reason: 至今太后发愤，一旦升遐 keeps a temporal/causal difficulty: whether 至今 frames continuing indignation into sudden death, and 升遐 as reported death, must not be silently emended or dated.
至今太后发愤，一旦升遐 keeps a temporal/causal difficulty: whether 至今 frames continuing indignation into sudden death, and 升遐 as reported death, must not be silently emended or dated.
